To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the actuator mass for a jet injection system powered by a permanent magnet motor scales with the square of the jet velocity divided by the motor efficiency, and that the actuator efficiency increases with the square root of the motor volume divided by the jet volume.
the mass of a jet injection device can be reduced to 0.6 kg by using a linear actuator that weighs 0.1 kg.
the mass of an electronically controlled jet injection system is inversely proportional to the jet velocity to the 3.5th power and to the volume of the injection to the 2.5th power.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a compact, portable jet injection system that can be powered using a small, lightweight, and low-power battery pack.
the optimization of the actuator for a portable electronically controlled needle-free jet injection system.
the development and optimization of a portable electronically controlled needle-free jet injection system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the design and optimization of a portable electronically controlled needle-free jet injection system is possible.
the scaling laws presented herein provide a useful tool for the design of jet injectors, and that the model is a good starting point for the design of any linear motor-powered jet injector.
the design of a portable electronically controlled needle-free jet injection system is possible and can be achieved by using the proposed scaling relationships and design guidelines.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed a scaling law for jet injection systems that can be used to optimize the size of portable jet injectors.
the mass of an injection device can be scaled down by increasing the motor efficiency, increasing the motor current density, and reducing the volume of the injection system.
the mass of a jet-injection system can be significantly reduced by optimizing the motor design, and that this reduction in size can be achieved without compromising performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a portable, electronically controlled, needle-free jet injection system is achievable.
the optimal actuator design for jet injection is highly dependent on injection volume and velocity.
the actuator mass scales with the square of the jet velocity, which means that the size of the actuator scales with jet velocity.
